item.title: Visualizing linear algebra
item.description: I wanted to learn Dirac’s equation, but linear algebra comes first. Seeing it visually made the concepts click in a way the formulas never did. Three views of a vector: Physics: an arrow in space, defined only by its length and direction. It can sit anywhere as long as those two stay the same. Computer science: an ordered list of numbers. A house could be the 2D vector (square footage, price). Order matters, and dimension is the length of the list. item.title: Bosons and Fermions
item.description: So I read a little about quantum computing and somehow ended up learning that every particle in the universe is either a boson or a fermion 😄 Fermions (electrons, protons, neutrons) have half integer spin and an antisymmetric wave function. Bosons (like photons) have integer spin and a symmetric wave function. One thing I found interesting: Helium 4 behaves as a boson because its total spin is 0. And then I suddenly remembered an episode from The Big Bang Theory 😄. Turns out those boson vs fermion jokes hit differently when you actually know what they are.

item.title: RSA is hard because factoring is hard, Quantum computing changes that!
item.description: Was reading about some quantum computing concepts today and stumbled upon Shor's Algorithm and Grover's Algorithm. I've always been curious about how quantum computing could threaten modern cryptography. Got to know that RSA's security basically relies on the fact that multiplying two large primes is easy, but finding the original primes from the result is extremely hard. Shor's Algorithm changes that by making factorization efficient on a quantum computer. Grover's Algorithm was interesting too.
